composition.story: A decision tree splits a fixed 10-point, two-feature plane greedily. At each node it scores every axis-aligned midpoint cut by weighted Gini impurity, keeps the lowest, and recurses into each side. Step through: x1 ≤ 5 wins the root, x2 ≤ 5.5 purifies the right box, leaving three rectangles. Finally, classify a new point.

aha.observation: Each split cuts one existing box along one feature axis, so the three pure leaves are exactly three nested, axis-aligned rectangles with Gini 0.

Trace attached to the step rail, marking completed states.
Left: x1–x2 plane (0–10 both axes, shared scale) with points, cuts and boxes. Right: tree nodes joined by labelled edges; box links connect leaves to rectangles.
Faded outline of the previous state's highlighted cut and boxes.
Anchored to the active cut or box; says where only, without numbers.
Panel below picture: counts, Gini formula, candidate cut, weighted Gini, gain; 3-decimal rounding.

controls.label: Step
controls.presentation: Previous / Next buttons, keep names when disabled at boundaries; arrow keys; visible focus.

variants.label: Gini, 10 points, midpoint thresholds, stop when pure

states.label: Root impurity
states.sentence: All 10 points share one region: 6 A, 4 B. Gini = 1 − (0.6² + 0.4²) = 0.48.
states.why: Impurity measures how mixed the region is; splits must lower it.

states.label: Try x1 = 3.5
states.sentence: Trial cut x1 = 3.5 leaves a pure left side but a mixed right side; weighted Gini 0.343.
states.why: Every midpoint between sorted feature values is scored the same way.

states.label: Try x1 = 5
states.sentence: Trial cut x1 = 5 isolates all four left A points; weighted Gini drops to 0.267, lowest of 14 candidates.
states.why: A larger pure side lowers the weighted average most.

states.label: Try x2 = 5
states.sentence: Best x2 cut, x2 = 5, scores 0.343; it loses to x1 = 5, so feature x1 wins the root.
states.why: Both features compete; the greedy rule keeps the single lowest score.

states.label: Commit x1 ≤ 5
states.sentence: The tree commits x1 ≤ 5: a vertical line splits the plane; the pure left box becomes a leaf.
states.why: A pure node needs no further split, so recursion stops there.

states.label: Recurse right
states.sentence: Recurse into the right box (2 A, 4 B, Gini 0.444). Cut x2 = 5.5 separates them perfectly: weighted Gini 0.
states.why: The same scan reruns using only the 6 points inside this box.

states.label: Three rectangles
states.sentence: Committing x2 ≤ 5.5 cuts only the right box. Three pure leaves equal three axis-aligned rectangles.
states.why: Each split subdivides one existing box along one axis, never the whole plane.

states.label: Classify (8, 6)
states.sentence: New point (8, 6) follows x1 > 5, then x2 > 5.5, landing in the upper-right box: class A.
states.why: Prediction is walking the tree, which equals finding the point's rectangle.
